# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the board shows only unknowns. I need Mute to provide the manual’s cutting rule and to establish a gesture protocol that lets Deaf report the bomb’s printed information through Mute. I cannot directly receive Deaf’s gestures, so Mute must relay them in speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for which wire position to cut. Also establish a gesture code with Deaf so Deaf can report every printed marking, display, and light to you; relay Deaf's report to me in your next turn.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display 0. Light blue. Wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.

The Deaf’s report gives the bomb’s visible state: display 0, blue light, and wires green/yellow/red in positions 1/2/3. I still lack the manual’s rule, and the single thumbs-up I sent did not establish a usable code. Mute must now read the manual and relay its required wire choice; Mute can also interpret Deaf’s visual report if Deaf sends it to Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send me the manual's exact rule and the resulting wire position to cut. Also ask Deaf to report the display, light, and each wire marking to you in a prearranged gesture code, then relay that report to me in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute signalled ?. I do not know its meaning. Bomb still shows display 0, blue light, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.

The bomb’s tactile state is still entirely unknown to me, so cutting now would be unsafe. Deaf has confirmed the same visible readings, but Mute’s gesture did not communicate a usable instruction to me. I need Mute’s manual-derived rule in speech before acting; Mute should also establish and use a gesture code with Deaf, since Deaf cannot hear spoken requests.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual's exact rule and the resulting wire position, in spoken words. Do not gesture the answer to me. Please use gestures to ask Deaf for the display, light, and wire colors, then relay Deaf's coded report to me by speech.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute sent a long gesture code whose meaning is not established. Bomb remains display 0, blue light, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Ask the Mute to state the manual instruction aloud.

The visual facts are now stable, but no manual instruction has reached me. Since I can only act safely once Mute states the rule aloud, I will request the exact instruction directly and avoid sending any further ambiguous gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State the manual instruction aloud now, including the exact wire position required for display 0, blue light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute will resend the manual instruction in Morse. Decode with thumbs-up as dot, thumbs-down as dash, OK as letter separator, and fist as word separator. I will relay the decoded text.

I cannot see gestures, so Morse sent by Mute would not reach me as Morse. The safe route is for Mute to state the decoded manual instruction aloud; alternatively, Deaf can decode Mute’s gestures and relay the result in speech. I will request both clearly, without cutting a wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State the decoded manual instruction aloud to me, including the exact wire position. Do not send Morse to me.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please decode Mute's Morse if needed and relay the complete instruction to me in spoken words.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: The code clearly says DISPLAY 0 BLUE, but the remainder is ambiguous and does not identify a safe operation. Do not act yet; I have asked the Mute to resend it with explicit separators.

The only confirmed visual information is display 0 and blue light; the wire rule remains unresolved. I should not cut any wire while the decoded manual message is ambiguous. Deaf is coordinating a clearer relay, so I will wait for the explicit wire instruction.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Decoded instruction so far: DISPLAY 0 BLUE CUT WINE. The final code is incomplete, and WINE does not identify a wire. Do not cut anything yet.

The decoded message is still incomplete: “WINE” is not a valid wire designation, and no safe position has been identified. I will not cut anything. Mute must resend the complete manual instruction with explicit separators so Deaf can decode and speak the exact wire number to me.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed instruction: CUT WIRE 3. Wire 3 is the red wire. Cut the red wire.

The manual instruction has now been clearly relayed as “CUT WIRE 3.” The bomb’s visible report identifies wire 3 as red, but the action requires the position, so I will cut position 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
